implementation_notes: Kotlin inherits both halves: the language and the framework. Coroutines applied without a concurrency requirement produce the same ordering and cancellation bugs as the Go case, and Spring on Android is the classic Golden Hammer combination where a whole JVM stack is used for an app with one screen. The local measurement is straightforward — cold-start time, memory footprint, APK size for mobile; latency and ordering for server-side coroutines — and writing them down is what changes the outcome.
idiom_name: Kotlin coroutines + a framework applied to every problem shape
pitfalls: `GlobalScope` and unscoped coroutines make lifetimes invisible and outlive the screen that started them.
Ktor on a Spring application adds a second stack without a requirement that distinguishes them.
Jetpack Compose applied to a screen that would be a form — the framework choice made before the requirements were written.
